chunks: 35 - Muhammad ibn Uthman narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Affan and Yahya ibn Ishaq as-Salihini narrated to us, they said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Uthman narrated from Abut-Tufayl
He said: Abdullah ibn Amr said to me: O Abut-Tufayl, count twelve from the sons of Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, then there will be the Nafq and the Naqaf.

key_terms.النَّقَاف: Naqaf, a term used in this context referring to the Imams
key_terms.النَّقْف: Nafq, a term used in this context referring to the Imams
key_terms.بَنِي كَعْبِ بْنِ لُؤَي: Sons of Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, a prominent clan of Quraysh

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of counting twelve from Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ay in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the prophetic designation of the Twelve Imams from the lineage of Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, a branch of Quraysh. The mention of 'Nafq and Naqaf' refers to specific terms or signs associated with their succession, underscoring the divine precision in selecting the Imams from the Prophet's direct descendants. This narration is foundational in Shia theology for establishing the number and lineage of the Imams as divinely ordained.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (35) Muhammad bin Uthman narrated from Ahmad from Affan and Yahya bin Iss’haq as-Saleheeni from Hammad bin Salama from Abdullah bin Uthman from Abut-Tufayl
that Abdullah bin Umar had said to him: “O Abut-Tufayl, Count twelve ones of bani Ka’b bin Lu’ay and then fighting and killing occur.”
